chunks: And by this same chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAli ibn Hadid and Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn ʿIsa, from Hariz ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Zurara, from Abu Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said:

The sunnah has been established regarding cleansing after defecation with three stones: that one wipes the perineum (ʿijān) without washing it; and it is permissible to wipe the feet without washing them.

key_terms.الْعِجَانَ: ʿijān — the perineum, area between genitals and anus
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the act of relieving oneself
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe, to perform masḥ (dry cleaning, as distinct from washing)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir (AS) say about cleaning after defecation with three stones, and is washing the perineum and feet obligatory in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the sunnah ruling on istinja' after defecation: three stones suffice for wiping the perineum (ʿijān) without washing it, and wiping the feet without washing them is likewise permissible. The hadith defines the minimum obligatory practice, distinguishing masḥ (dry wiping) from ghusl (washing) in post-defecation purification—a key fiqh distinction rooted in early Islamic bodily-purity law.
